title: CLOCKS Pulse BUILD - 26 resident loops to one 15s tick, pool-only claim, calendar --once
applies_to: the live COSMOS tree; COW applies, this lane does not

context_gaps.detail: docs/AGENT_BRIEF.md, docs/AGENT_BOUNDARIES.md and docs/ORCHESTRATION.md are named by the work order but exist on NO branch of github.com/keithbbf-gif/cosmos as of 2026-09-04. They were not read. Absent is not empty and not read: the boundaries used here are the ones stated verbatim in the work order and issue #34, plus docs/WORK_ORDER_SOP.md and docs/AGENTS.md, which ARE in the clone.
context_gaps.consequence: Any boundary that lives only in the three missing files is UNCHECKED by this proposal. Publish them to the repo (or paste them into the order) before COW accepts.

context_gaps.detail: cosmos_own_clocks.py, cosmos_health_clock.py, cosmos_pool.py, cosmos_run.py, cosmos_cdeck_feed.py, cosmos_index.py and cosmos_principles.py are live-tree modules and are not in this repo. The 26 clock NAMES were therefore never seen.
context_gaps.consequence: This manifest ships UNBOUND and proposals/pulse/pulse_bind.py REFUSES it until COW binds every live clock name. Fail-closed by construction: a plan that guessed the names would silently not run the real ones.

never: apply any of this from the Cursor lane

pulse.tick_s_rationale: 15s is the tightest cadence already live in the tree (the ~15s Work-Order Runner schtask, docs/WORK_ORDER_SOP.md step 3). The collapse must not lengthen the tightest cadence, and a grid finer than the tightest need buys nothing but wakeups.
pulse.tick_budget_rationale: One third of the period for in-process work. Anything that can exceed it is dispatched as a --once child, so the wheel cannot be held hostage by one slow clock.
pulse.grid: deadlines are t0 + n*tick from a monotonic origin; a slow tick never pushes the grid, so drift cannot accumulate
pulse.catch_up_rationale: A Pulse that was down for an hour must not fire 240 backlogged ticks on resume. At most one catch-up per clock; the missed count is REPORTED as skew.
pulse.quantization: effective_period = ceil(declared_period / tick) * tick. A clock whose cadence the grid CHANGES must declare max_interval_s - the largest gap its duty tolerates. No declaration is a refusal (QUANTIZATION_UNDECLARED), and a tolerance the grid cannot meet is a refusal (QUANTIZATION_EXCEEDS_TOLERANCE). deadline_s is a different field: how long ONE run may take before it is STALE. Conflating the two refuses a nightly job for having a short runtime deadline.
pulse.phase_offsets: deterministic, sha1(clock_id) % slots - two boots and two lanes agree, and 26 clocks do not pile onto one tick

heartbeat.primary: one file, every clock, per tick: writer identity + epoch + UTC + aware-local + tz offset + tick_seq + per-clock state, last_run_epoch, residency and stale_after_s
heartbeat.states_rationale: absent != unreadable != changed != empty; NEVER-RUN is not stale and not green
heartbeat.legacy_shim: the same tick data re-emitted under the per-daemon filenames the cDeck glob and index already watch, so no reader goes red because a writer changed
heartbeat.shim_retirement: shim is parked (not deleted) only after every reader has run one full day on the primary file

claims.surface: pool.claim_next - the ONLY code path that may transition a work item to claimed
claims.loser: typed LOST_CLAIM, counted, non-fatal; the tick moves on

negative_control.contract: must report BROKE on every tick; a CLEAN here publishes verdict PULSE-BROKEN and no green is reported
negative_control.rationale: a wheel with no planted failure has never been seen to fail

refusals_at_boot: UNBOUND_PLAN - an empty wheel that starts is a silent outage

classification.note: Deterministic predicate, applied in order. Two lanes running it on the same registry must land on the same disposition; a judgement call that differs per reader is how a collapse drifts.

rules.if: holds a listening socket or is the Core service

rules.then: resident.keep until the phase that grants Core spawn to Pulse

rules.if: spawns_core and Pulse does not hold the spawn lease
needs sub-minute latency and typical cost < 250ms and no blocking IO
period >= 900s and tolerates a missed window
duty fully absorbed by another clock
rules.then: parked (registry entry RETAINED, schtask disabled and renamed _delme, never deleted)

classification.hold_rule: hold_required clocks (the collector tick) run under HOLD; every discretionary clock is skipped with reason HOLD and the skip is recorded. HOLD is not lifted by this build and the collector's tick requirement is not modified by it.

residency_target.plus: COSMOS Core (:8770) stays the resident Windows service it already is
residency_target.note: 26 entries in, 26 entries out. Residency changes; the registry does not shrink.

role_slots.note: Roles this lane can name from in-repo evidence. COW binds each to the real clock id at apply time; the binder refuses any slot left null.

slots.evidence: work order: 'Collector tick already required under HOLD'
slots.note: required under HOLD; this build does not change that requirement

slots.evidence: work order: only in-tree restarter of live Core

slots.note: the negative control is a NEW clock, added to the wheel, not taken from the 26

bindings.how: COW exports the live registry read-only as {"clocks": [...]} and runs: python proposals/pulse/pulse_bind.py --plan proposals/clocks-pulse-build.json --live-clocks <export>. Exit 2 until every name is bound.

couplings.today: each resident loop writes its own heartbeat file
couplings.target: Pulse writes one heartbeat carrying all 26 clocks, each with state + last_run_epoch + stale_after_s
couplings.shim: legacy per-clock filenames re-emitted from the same tick data during the collapse window
couplings.gate: no reader observes a heartbeat gap longer than its own stale_after_s across the cutover

couplings.today: written by each daemon; the key set is the daemon set
couplings.target: same key set, same shape, written by Pulse with via='pulse' and owner_pid added
couplings.shim: keys are NOT removed; a peer that reads a key it has always read keeps reading it
couplings.gate: peer-side diff of the key set before/after is empty

couplings.today: globs the heartbeat directory for per-daemon files
couplings.target: reads the primary heartbeat's clocks[] behind a feature flag
couplings.shim: glob keeps working against shim files; both paths measured side by side for one full day before the flag flips
couplings.gate: flag-on and flag-off panels agree for a full day, then the shim is parked

couplings.today: liveness = a process exists for each of N daemon entries
couplings.target: liveness = the clock TICKED within stale_after_s; each entry gains a residency field (resident|pulse|calendar)
couplings.shim: the list is not shortened; parked entries report residency=pulse and are green when their clock ticks
couplings.gate: index green with the same entry count (26) and no entry removed

couplings.target: 2 Logon entries: COSMOS Pulse and COSMOS Health --supervise
couplings.shim: the other 11 are /change /disable'd and renamed under _delme; registered, reversible with /change /enable, never deleted
couplings.gate: schtasks /query /xml read-back shows 2 enabled Logon triggers and 11 disabled-but-present

couplings.today: five code paths can claim work
couplings.target: pool.claim_next is the only claimant; the other four become thin adapters that call it
couplings.shim: adapters keep their public signatures so callers do not change in the same step
couplings.gate: a guard test proves no module outside the pool performs a claim rename or claim ledger append; an overlap test shows zero double-claims and at least one typed LOST_CLAIM

schtasks.name: COSMOS Work-Order Runner
schtasks.why: its 15s duty becomes the Pulse cadence; the task stays registered so /change /enable is the entire rollback

schtasks.name: <11 parked Logon relaunch tasks - bind names at apply>
schtasks.read_back: schtasks /query /xml over the whole folder, entry count unchanged

schtasks.name: COSMOS Health Supervise
schtasks.why: the only in-tree restarter of live Core :8770; untouched until P5

phases.name: Shadow - observe, dispatch nothing
phases.does: Pulse runs alongside the 26 loops in dry-run: it computes the due set and writes a SHADOW heartbeat under a distinct name. It dispatches nothing and claims nothing.
phases.gate: for one full day, the shadow due-set reproduces every observed live run for all 26 clocks within one tick; any clock whose real cadence disagrees with its declared period is re-declared before P1
phases.rollback: stop the shadow process; nothing else changed

phases.name: Leaf clocks - Pulse takes the ones with no claim surface and no Core dependency
phases.does: register COSMOS Pulse; leaf loops exit on a PULSE_OWNED flag file; their 11 Logon tasks are disabled and renamed _delme; the legacy heartbeat shim goes on
phases.gate: heartbeat continuity for every moved clock (no gap > stale_after_s); index green at 26 entries; cDeck glob green; schtasks read-back shows the parked tasks still registered
phases.rollback: delete the PULSE_OWNED flag and schtasks /change /enable the 11 parked tasks - the loops come back on next Logon or on demand

phases.name: Calendar migration - --once triggers, registered and read back
phases.does: clocks matching classification rule 6 move to Task Scheduler calendar triggers invoking <module> --once
phases.gate: each new trigger read back with /query /xml AND observed to fire once before its old loop is stood down
phases.rollback: disable the calendar trigger, re-enable the parked loop task

phases.name: Claim collapse - five surfaces become one pool.claim_next
phases.does: the four non-pool surfaces become adapters over pool.claim_next; Pulse drains the pool at most 4 claims per tick; the ~15s Work-Order Runner task is disabled and its cadence is served by the wheel
phases.gate: overlap test: zero double-claims across concurrent claimants; at least one typed LOST_CLAIM observed (a claim path that has never lost is a claim path nobody has seen contend); guard test proves no claim outside the pool; work-order end-to-end latency no worse than the 15s baseline
phases.rollback: re-enable the Work-Order Runner task; adapters keep their old bodies behind a flag for one release

phases.name: Collector under HOLD - required tick preserved
phases.does: the collector tick runs on the wheel with hold_required=true, so it fires while HOLD is set and every discretionary clock is skipped with a recorded reason
phases.gate: with HOLD set, the collector's tick count over an hour equals the pre-collapse count; every skipped clock carries reason HOLD; HOLD itself is untouched
phases.rollback: return the collector to its own loop; the flag file is the switch

phases.name: Core spawn handoff - Health --supervise hands the restarter role to Pulse
phases.does: Pulse takes a single-owner spawn lease with a fencing token; Health --supervise stops spawning only after the lease read-back confirms Pulse holds it. Core itself is never stopped: this transfers who would restart it, not whether it runs.
phases.gate: the lease is single-owner under a forced contention test; :8770 answers on every 15s sample across the whole handoff window with zero misses; a deliberate Core kill in a REHEARSAL instance (never live) is restarted by Pulse within the same window Health achieved
phases.rollback: release the lease; Health --supervise resumes as restarter on its next tick. This phase is last precisely because it is the only one that can lose the restarter.

rollback.principle: nothing is deleted, so every phase reverses with one verb
steps: remove the PULSE_OWNED flag file - the loops resume owning their duty
schtasks /change /enable each parked task (they were never /delete'd, only disabled and renamed _delme)
disable COSMOS Pulse; Health --supervise is still the Core restarter unless P5 committed
if P5 committed: release the spawn lease and Health resumes on its next tick
the CLOCKS registry needs no rollback: it was never shrunk

open_questions: The three named context docs are missing from the repo - publish them or the boundary set stays partly unchecked.
Which of the 26 clocks tolerate a missed window? That predicate decides pulse.once vs calendar.once and only the live owner can answer it per clock.

What gap does each clock actually tolerate (max_interval_s)? Every clock whose period is not already a multiple of 15s needs that number from its owner, and the binder refuses until it has one. A clock that tolerates less than 15s cannot be Pulse-owned at this grid at all.
Does any non-pool claim surface hold state the pool does not model (lane, priority, attempt-private workspace)? P3 blocks until that is answered.
